findings.resolution: First-use SGLT2 class now explains urinary glucose removal in both languages, with actual-read NHS Scotland mechanism support only.
Author repair before independent review correctly states suspected DKA stopping and urgent evaluation, with no self-restart. MHRA wording and independent joint consensus scope read.
Clinically significant cerebral edema is explicitly differentiated from subclinical swelling; adult consensus and pediatric RCH scopes read.
New mechanism source included in the condition top-level source list; this is citation closure only, with no new medical claim.

sections.assessment: Insulin deficiency, ketones and acidosis distinguished; type1/type2 and first-presentation scope correct; coma is a possible severe manifestation, not necessary for emergency care.
Illness/insulin omission/pump interruption and SGLT2 risk retain source boundaries. First-use urinary-glucose mechanism now understandable and precisely sourced; lower glucose does not exclude DKA.
Dangerous symptoms require prompt emergency evaluation; neither home testing nor very high glucose is prerequisite. Pregnancy/children and dehydration alter urgency; no home dose algorithm.

NHS/Diabetes UK >3 mmol/L is explicitly UK guidance, not diagnosis or a universal threshold. US ADA differs; early symptoms and agreed lower escalation thresholds override waiting. Cannot contact team/worsening requires emergency pathway.
Clinical blood acidity/ketones and electrolyte evaluation distinguished from glucose or home urine result alone; cause investigation and cautious recovery interpretation preserved.

Ordinary fasting ketosis, HHS, low glucose and other illness differentiated without encouraging self-exclusion. Persistent abdominal pain after acidosis resolves has original publisher and consensus/Merck context.

Monitored hospital insulin/fluids/electrolytes, trigger treatment and dextrose while clearing ketones explained; outcome benefit not guaranteed or quantified beyond source. Children and comorbid volume limits preserved.

Insulin/potassium/dextrose roles and monitoring risks accurately paired. MHRA suspected-DKA stopping advice plus independently written consensus admission/no-routine-restart support no self-restart; no ordinary universal stop-insulin instruction.

Hydration and food choices tied to ability to retain intake and personal plan; vomiting/inability to drink invokes urgent care rather than prolonged home attempts. SGLT2 fasting/low-carb risk preserved, no universal food ban.
Glucose/ketone recording, supply dates, pump backup and identification are ordinary practical organization. Device-specific doses are not generalized, and persistent signs require escalation.

Children, pregnancy, older/cardiac and advanced renal patients have explicitly different monitoring/volume concerns. NICE/RCH and adult consensus/renal review supply population-specific scope; no adult rates imported into children.

Recovery depends on resolving acidosis/ketones and triggers rather than glucose alone. Recurrence prevention, access costs and psychological support are practical follow-up without a fabricated benefit percentage.

Dehydration, electrolyte shifts, hypoglycemia and neurologic decline retain immediate-care implications. Clinically significant cerebral edema is distinguished from subclinical swelling; no claim that all cerebral swelling is rare in children.

Sick-day plans, prescribed insulin continuation, ketone access and pump backup remain component-specific. Broad sick-day pill statements do not override SGLT2 exceptions; practical plans are not represented as guaranteed prevention.

bilingual_assessment: Current64 claims read as bilingual pairs; populations, qualifications, timing, actions and numerical units match. No extra English-only or Chinese-only permission to delay care or self-dose identified.
independence_assessment: Same-institution pages are one source family; the joint consensus is one writing rather than five society sources. MHRA and EMA share upstream safety assessment. Mayo, Merck, Diabetes UK, RCH and pump handbooks disclose shared clinical references where relevant, and are not called independent experiments. UK/US threshold disagreement is attributed, not erased. Ordinary recordkeeping and low-risk information organization do not acquire fabricated second citations.
resolution: Accepted for the14-section bilingual lay DKA overview. Source scope, date, retrieval limits and population boundaries retained; critical action/risk evidence checked at component level. No clinical sign-off or ICD category expansion follows from this editorial acceptance.
scope_limits: No individualized insulin, fluid, potassium or home-correction doses.
Not a complete pediatric, obstetric or end-stage kidney failure treatment protocol.
Home ketone escalation is not an acid-base diagnostic definition; modest glucose does not exclude DKA.
Indexed-only sources and partial original publisher passages are explicitly labeled, not attested as full-document reads.

validation.review_placeholder_handling: Only the exact pending-independent-review placeholder was resolved in the in-memory candidate probe; original draft records remain pending.
